body:
That should mean that similar to how /fix does, we do ask for deep analysis, create an issue with actual GitHub native sub-issues, that includes all open issues in the repository, and produce single pull request draft as /solve command would normally do, but for single issue, which will contain all open issues.

So we get all open issues, create a new issue list them as sub issues (if we hit the limit, we should add 100 (or whatever the limit) oldest only, and ignore others).

After that issue is created we just pass it to /solve instead.

So in such case we should be able to close lots of open issues at once with single big pull request, so as the result of merging all these issues including the combined issue will be closed.

The only difference is in the process of checking pull request we double check that pull request description will have exactly all the issues listed.

Also for any other single issue, we should have `--ensure-all-sub-issues-addressed` (which we also will use here internally). This `--ensure-all-sub-issues-addressed` option works like this - it checks if all issues listed in pull request as proper GitHub recognized references, if not we auto-resume/auto-restart and ask do double check if all issues were addressed in this single pull request.

We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
title: Allow to pass repository link to `/solve` commands
